title: Brain-heart coupling in tourette syndrome: a precision functional mapping study of discordant siblings.
reviewer: dot; single-assistant extraction, not independent clinical peer review

correction_retraction_check.result: No linked CommentsCorrections notice in the retrieved PubMed XML; focused 1-9 October entry-date correction/retraction query returned zero records.

design: Small observational precision-functional-mapping pilot; repeated resting fMRI and concurrent pulse recordings in two TS-discordant sibling pairs.
population: Children with Tourette syndrome and unaffected siblings; published aggregate study description only.
comparator: Unaffected siblings; within-participant repeated physiological/network measurements.
intervention_exposure: No treatment intervention; pulse-derived RMSSD and time-varying functional connectivity.
outcomes: Two targeted sets of autonomic-network coupling analyses; independent preregistration not verified.
followup: Repeated scanning sessions; no sustained-remission or treatment-withdrawal follow-up.
key_result: Individual autonomic-network association patterns differed; evidence is descriptive and hypothesis-generating.
uncertainty: Only four independent participants; repeated windows are dependent. Tics were not independently annotated, respiration was unmeasured, and clinical heterogeneity limits TS-specific inference.
inference_not_supported: An autonomic signal precedes or causes tics; a validated tic predictor, remission mechanism, treatment effect or cure.
adverse_events: Clinical safety was not established; adverse-event extraction not performed for this non-treatment study.
attrition: Participant recruitment/exclusion flow not fully extracted; repeated-window quality control does not establish participant-level retention.
funding: Kavli Institute for Brain and Mind postdoctoral award, Tourette Association of America and NSF Graduate Research Fellowship Program, as reported in the paper.
conflicts: Authors report no commercial or financial relationships constituting a potential conflict.
retrieval_status: Publisher full-text methods, results interpretation, limitations and disclosures inspected; no raw-data reanalysis.
related_cohort_note: Participants came from an ongoing UC San Diego precision-functional-mapping study. Overlap with other cohort publications was not resolved.
next_verification_task: Require concurrent tic annotation, respiratory/cardiac controls and held-out temporal prediction before promoting an autonomic-precursor hypothesis; verify participant/cohort independence in later syntheses.

population: Adults with chronic tic disorder and neurotypical adults.

outcomes: P50, N140 and P300 gating indices; relation to self-reported tactile responsivity. Preregistration not verified.

inference_not_supported: A universal sensory-gating deficit in CTD, absence of every gating abnormality, or a validated treatment/remission target.
